blocks.text: Verses 9–11 recall God’s power over the sea and picture the redeemed returning to Zion with singing. This imagery is often read within Isaiah 40–55’s announcement of comfort and return from Babylon, drawing on creation and exodus language to portray a new homecoming. That hopeful picture does not, by itself, mean that the trauma of displacement or conflict after return has simply disappeared.

The Great Isaiah Scroll preserves almost the entire sixty-six-chapter book and is broadly aligned with the Masoretic tradition, though it includes thousands of spelling and substantive differences. Other Isaiah manuscripts and interpretive writings from Qumran also show that Isaiah was actively copied and interpreted.
